name: System/SDK <-> reality parity -- establish + close how faithfully infra/system + sdk represent Opal's live engineering, ontology, comp-tools, and infrastructure, and convert parity-maintenance from care into a control
description: Andrew-direct 2026-07-19 (VERBATIM): 'is /system, and the underlying /sdk folder, completely representative of how the engineering, ontology, comp tools, infrastructure, etc actually work in reality? ... do a comprehensive analysis to that end first to establish how close these folders represent the reality of the system so as to attempt to reach parity. write a brief on that and issue to CTO for an NFRA_SYSPARITY project.' MSTR ran a 4-domain grounded analysis (4 independent analysts + MSTR live-verification of the load-bearing findings). FINDING: the architecture representation is high-fidelity and self-aware, but parity is held by CARE (hand-passes + on-demand sweeps that have LAPSED), not a CONTROL -- the CHECK-LIVE-NOT-FROZEN doctrine (LD-0314) on the system's own self-description. The gap is UNEVEN: comp-tools ~85% / infrastructure ~80% (fresh but never cloud-exercised, Rule 22a) / engineering+loops ~70-75% (06_current_state 250 commits stale, comp-system --check = SYSTEM STALE) / ontology ~40% (absent from the 8 core docs; SDK v0.1 stub; 06 reports cse_schema 0.4 while live is 0.5; the drift-gate is BLIND to RULE_BANK.yaml -- the LD-0314 self-referential hole confirmed at its live instance). SYSPARITY = the baseline audit + the make-parity-a-CONTROL project (gate the 06 refresh, complete the drift-gate denominator, represent the ontology, exercise the SDK at cloud tier or rule local-only sufficient, SLA the incorporation debt). Distinct from NFRA_NESTEDABSTRACT (forward incorporation) -- SYSPARITY measures + closes the ACCUMULATED gap and checks whether the maintenance controls are even sufficient. Part 2 = NFRA_ONTOCLARITY (a separate ontology semantic-clarity audit; 10 fog-spots seeded).
